what: External Dataset Survey, Hybrid Architecture Phase 2A (Issue #51). Discovery and verification only: nothing was integrated, mixed with V4-clean or used for training. Checked 2026-10-01.

verification_levels.measured: statistic computed by scripts/dataset/survey_external_datasets.py on the actual files (external_datasets_measurements.json)

verification_levels.secondary: only from a secondary description (search summary, mirror, third-party README); stated as such

datasets.name: SR-BH 2020 multi-label dataset
datasets.host_vs_origin: origin: Harvard Dataverse deposit by the authors; Kaggle (natasa213/data-capec-multilabel) and GitHub skolpin/SR-BH-2020-web-attack-dataset are mirrors / third-party analyses
datasets.authors: Sureda Riera T. (Universidad de Alcalá), Bermejo Higuera J.R., Bermejo Higuera J. (UNIR), et al.
datasets.publication: A new multi-label dataset for Web attacks CAPEC classification using machine learning techniques, Computers & Security, doi:10.1016/j.cose.2022.102788
datasets.date_version: deposited 2022-06-06, Dataverse version 1.2; traffic collected 12 days of July 2020
datasets.records: 907,815 rows parsed (measured); the deposit states 907,814 — 1-row difference not explained
datasets.format: CSV, 38 columns: 24 request/response fields + 14 binary label columns
datasets.real_or_synthetic: real Internet traffic to a WordPress honeypot (primary description)
datasets.unit: full requests decomposed into fields (method, request target, protocol, selected headers, body) plus response status/length
datasets.labels: 000 Normal + 13 CAPEC ids: 272 Protocol Manipulation, 242 Code Injection, 88 OS Command Injection, 126 Path Traversal, 66 SQL Injection, 16 Dictionary-based Password Attack, 310 Scanning for Vulnerable Software, 153 Input Data Manipulation, 248 Command Injection, 274 HTTP Verb Tampering, 194 Fake the Source of Data, 34 HTTP Response Splitting, 33 HTTP Request Smuggling
datasets.headers: fixed subset only: User-Agent, Referer, Host, Origin, Cookie, Content-Type, Accept, Accept-Language, Accept-Encoding, DNT, Connection — no Authorization, no Content-Length, no Transfer-Encoding (measured from the header row)
datasets.path_query_body: yes / yes (inside request target) / yes (26,743 non-empty bodies, measured)
datasets.source_metadata: src/dst ip and port; src_ip is 172.26.0.1 for all but 2 rows (measured) — no client attribution
datasets.deduplicated: no: only 378,627 distinct (method, target, body) among 907,815 rows (measured)
datasets.methodology: documented in the deposit and the paper: ModSecurity 2.9.2 + CRS 3.3.0 in detection-only mode, labels reviewed manually and semi-automatically, VM restored daily
datasets.repository: Dataverse deposit (no code repository from the authors found)
datasets.leakage_risks: labels derive from CRS detections (D9 circularity for any rule-vs-ML comparison); response fields (status, content length) are not available inline and must never be inputs; heavy duplication; 99.6% one Host (test-site.com) and one application
datasets.limitations: one WordPress site; SQL Injection is 250,311 of the attack labels; CAPEC-248 has 1 row; smuggling labels without the framing headers that constitute the attack; CAPEC taxonomy differs from V4's
datasets.fit_for_firewall_ia: compatible with the D1 representation after rendering fields to text (headers partial); RequestFeatures v2 computable from method/target/content-type/body; useful for `attack` and, after a CAPEC mapping, partly for categories; rare categories (response splitting, smuggling, verb tampering, protocol manipulation); real multi-label evidence; licence clean

datasets.name: ECML/PKDD 2007 Discovery Challenge — Analyzing Web Traffic
datasets.host_vs_origin: origin: LIRMM challenge site (data link 'Donnees'); github.com/msudol/Web-Application-Attack-Datasets is a GPL-3.0 mirror of ECML/PKDD 2007 + CSIC 2010
datasets.authors: LIRMM and EMA LGI2P with Bee Ware; description paper Raïssi C., Brissaud J., Dray G., Poncelet P., Roche M., Teisseire M.
datasets.publication: Web Analyzing Traffic Challenge: Description and Results, ECML/PKDD 2007 Discovery Challenge, pp. 47-52
datasets.license: none stated on the challenge page or in the paper (unverified)
datasets.size: about 50,000 samples, about 20% attacks (challenge page); 35,006 valid / 15,110 attacks (secondary: GSI web-application-attacks-datasets README)
datasets.format: XML; per sample: context, class, query
datasets.real_or_synthetic: traffic provided with Bee Ware; the paper states attacks 'are constructed blindly'; URLs, parameter names and values were replaced by random strings (secondary)
datasets.unit: full requests: method, protocol, uri, query, headers, body (primary paper)
datasets.labels: one 'type' per sample: Valid, XSS, SqlInjection, LdapInjection, XPathInjection, PathTransversal, OsCommanding, SSI; 'inContext' flag; 'attackIntervall' giving the element (uri, query, body or header name) and character interval of the attack
datasets.headers: yes (primary paper); attacks can be located in a named header
datasets.multi_label: the paper says a sample 'can eventually target several classes', but the format records one type (unverified whether any sample carries more)
datasets.source_metadata: server context: OS, HTTP server, XPath / LDAP / SQL availability
datasets.leakage_risks: random-string values make lexical statistics unrealistic; attack location labels make an easy evaluation target but say nothing about real values
datasets.limitations: 2007-era attacks, sanitized values, licence unclear, contextual labels (inContext) differ from a pure request label
datasets.fit_for_firewall_ia: full requests with headers map to D1 text; categories LDAP and XPath are scarce in V4-clean; attack-location labels are the only public evidence found that marks header-borne attacks

datasets.name: OWASP CRS regression tests
datasets.host_vs_origin: origin: the OWASP CRS project repository
datasets.authors: OWASP Core Rule Set project contributors
datasets.publication: none (project documentation: coreruleset.org testing docs; go-ftw framework)
datasets.format: YAML (go-ftw): per test, HTTP request (method, uri, headers, data, or a raw/encoded request) and the expected rule ids
datasets.real_or_synthetic: synthetic, hand-written to trigger or not trigger specific rules
datasets.benign_malicious: both: 1,018 stages are false-positive regression tests (only no_expect_ids)
datasets.headers: yes; 10 raw or encoded requests for malformed framing (measured)
datasets.multi_label: no in practice: 1 stage expects more than one rule id (measured)
datasets.source_metadata: rule family per directory (920 protocol enforcement, 921 protocol attack, 930 LFI, 931 RFI, 932 RCE, 941 XSS, 942 SQLi, ...)
datasets.deduplicated: not a goal; overlapping payloads across rules likely
datasets.leakage_risks: labels are rule ids: training on them learns CRS (D9); payloads chosen to hit specific regexes
datasets.limitations: test fixtures, not traffic; class balance meaningless
datasets.fit_for_firewall_ia: full requests incl. header- and framing-borne cases (921 protocol attacks: response splitting, header injection, smuggling); useful as a targeted evaluation of what RequestFeatures cannot see

datasets.name: A Thirty-Day Dataset of Malicious HTTP Requests Blocked by OWASP ModSecurity on a Production Web Server
datasets.host_vs_origin: origin: Zenodo deposit by the author; data paper in MDPI Data
datasets.authors: Lucz G. (Budapest University of Technology and Economics)
datasets.format: native ModSecurity audit log (sections A, B request line + headers, C body, F response, H rule messages), one file per day
datasets.labels: CRS rule messages with ids and tags (attack-lfi, attack-protocol, attack-sqli, attack-rce, ...)
datasets.benign_malicious: malicious / flagged only — no benign traffic
datasets.headers: all request headers as received (anonymized): Authorization 40, Cookie 5,367, Content-Length 14,706, Transfer-Encoding 20 (measured)
datasets.path_query_body: yes / yes / yes (13,071 with a body section, measured)
datasets.multi_label: multiple rule matches per request: 8,194 transactions carry ≥2 attack-family tags (5.7%; measured), mostly lfi + protocol (6,836)
datasets.session_info: anonymized addresses and timestamps could allow approximate grouping (unverified)
datasets.methodology: data paper (not read in full: MDPI returned 403)
datasets.leakage_risks: labels are CRS detections; only detected requests are present (undetected attacks cannot appear); anonymization tokens may create artificial regularities
datasets.limitations: no benign class; 47,613 transactions carry no attack-family tag; family mix dominated by lfi (49,800) and protocol (43,839)
datasets.fit_for_firewall_ia: full requests with real headers; evaluation of `attack` recall on real attack traffic and of header-borne cases; multi-rule evidence

datasets.name: WordPress Web Attack Audit Log Dataset (ModSec-WP)
datasets.host_vs_origin: origin: Zenodo deposit by the author
datasets.real_or_synthetic: controlled testbed: benign traffic and attacks against real WordPress plugin vulnerabilities replayed against a live site
datasets.unit: request line + body; ModSecurity message fields; response
datasets.labels: single label: sqli 69,631, normal 12,597, xss 8,625, bruteforce 7,568, fileinclusion-ldf 6,290, rce 4,172 (measured); hybrid labelling: scenario timestamps, regex matching, manual validation
datasets.headers: only Host and User-Agent (both excluded by D44)
datasets.source_metadata: remote address, ModSecurity rule id / message / severity per row
datasets.leakage_risks: the ModSecurity columns (message_rule_id, message_msg, ...) encode a detector's verdict and must never be inputs; regex-based labels
datasets.limitations: one platform; strong class imbalance; File Inclusion family merges LFI, RFI and path traversal
datasets.fit_for_firewall_ia: request line + body map to RequestFeatures; no header evidence; its File Inclusion family independently groups LFI/RFI/path traversal, as D49 does

datasets.name: GoTestWAF test cases
datasets.records: 168 payload entries in 44 YAML files (3 not parseable as YAML), expanded at run time by encoders x placeholders (measured)
datasets.format: YAML: payloads, encoders, placeholders (URLParam, HTMLForm, HTMLMultipartForm, JSONRequest, URLPath, RawRequest, XMLBody, GraphQL, Header, UserAgent, gRPC)
datasets.labels: test-set / category per file (crlf, ldap-injection, mail-injection, nosql-injection, path-traversal, rce, shell-injection, sql-injection, ss-include, sst-injection, xml-injection, graphql, ...); false-pos set of 47 texts
datasets.headers: via the Header and UserAgent placeholders (2 and 1 test files)
datasets.leakage_risks: combinatorial variants of very few payloads
datasets.limitations: a WAF test tool, not a dataset
datasets.fit_for_firewall_ia: robustness / placement / encoding evaluation, incl. rare categories (SSI, LDAP, NoSQL, SSTI, CRLF)

datasets.name: HTTP DATASET CSIC 2010
datasets.host_vs_origin: origin: CSIC (Spanish Research National Council); mirrors on Kaggle and GitHub
datasets.authors: CSIC (individual authors not verified in this survey)
datasets.size: 36,000 normal training + 36,000 normal test + about 25,000 anomalous (secondary); the local copy used by V4 is documented in docs/data_sources.md
datasets.format: raw HTTP requests (V4 used a CSV export)
datasets.real_or_synthetic: automatically generated for one e-commerce application
datasets.deduplicated: no (V4 had to group digit variants, D16)
datasets.leakage_risks: ALREADY A V4-CLEAN SOURCE: any reuse overlaps V4 train/eval and the Analyzer's internal test
datasets.limitations: no attack categories (V4 derived them with a keyword heuristic, F6); single application

datasets.name: CSIC TORPEDA 2012
datasets.host_vs_origin: origin: CSIC TORPEDA framework; no verified mirror
datasets.authors: Torrano-Giménez C., Pérez A., Álvarez G. (secondary)
datasets.format: XML with label and request (method, protocol, path, headers, body) (secondary)
datasets.labels: 10 classes: Normal, SQLi, Format String, Buffer Overflow, XPath, XSS, CRLFi, SSI, LDAP, Anomalous (secondary)
datasets.leakage_risks: same producer and generation approach as CSIC 2010, a V4 source; overlap unknown
datasets.limitations: primary source not reachable; all properties secondary
datasets.fit_for_firewall_ia: would cover CRLF, SSI, LDAP, XPath with headers — if the primary source and licence can be verified

datasets.name: HttpParamsDataset
datasets.records: norm 19,304 / anom 11,763: sqli 10,852, xss 532, cmdi 89, path-traversal 290 (README)
datasets.real_or_synthetic: benign values from CSIC 2010; attacks generated with sqlmap, XSSYA, Vega and FuzzDB
datasets.leakage_risks: benign values come from CSIC 2010, a V4 source
datasets.fit_for_firewall_ia: not representable as a D1 request without inventing the rest of the request

datasets.host_vs_origin: paper; dataset hosting not confirmed on the pages read
datasets.authors: Chatzoglou E., Kouliaridis V., Kambourakis G., Karopoulos G., Gritzalis S.
datasets.license: paper CC BY 4.0 on arXiv; dataset licence unverified

datasets.name: Small curated payload collections (e.g. SunnyThakur25/Web-Application-Payloads-Dataset, mirrored on Kaggle as cyberprince/web-application-payloads-dataset)

searched_without_a_usable_result.JWT attacks: no public labelled dataset of JWT attacks in HTTP requests found; only tutorials and CVE write-ups. CRS regression tests contain 5 tests whose description mentions JWT.
searched_without_a_usable_result.Request smuggling: no HTTP/1.1 request-level dataset that keeps the framing headers; SR-BH 2020 labels CAPEC-33 without Content-Length / Transfer-Encoding; H23Q is HTTP/2-3; CRS tests contain a handful of raw framing cases
searched_without_a_usable_result.CSRF: no labelled request-level dataset found (CRS: 1 test description)
